title: Launch Signal Sentinel — Compact Readiness Sheet
summary: Compact single-sheet playbook for preflight, canary, and ramp decisions. Focused on measurable signals (latency percentiles, error budget burn, quality regressions) and fast human+automation decision steps. Designed to be pinboard-ready for on-call and launch room.
objectives: Validate end-to-end request path under representative production load
Confirm no quality regressions vs baseline eval set (prompt-suite A)
Hold 99th pct latency < 450ms for 95% of traffic during ramp phases
Ensure cost per 1k tokens stays within budgeted delta (+/- 15%)
Provide clear automated rollback triggers and owner runbook
launch_timeline: T-14 to T-7: preflight tests (synthetic traffic, smoke, integration)
T-6 to T-3: closed canary (1% traffic), daily kpi review and quality checks
T-2 to T-0: staged ramp to 10% with surge and fallback rehearsals
Go window: progressive ramp (10 -> 30 -> 60 -> 100) with 1h stabilization at each step
Post-go (D+0 to D+7): heightened monitoring and 4x daily syncs until metrics stabilize
readiness_checklist: All feature flags implemented and verified in staging and prod namespaces
Canary routing policy configured in routing layer and smoke endpoints available
Observability: dashboards for per-route token cost, latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, and model-quality deltas deployed
Synthetic prompt-suite A uploaded and baseline eval scores recorded (id: EVAL-981)
Alerting: runbook-linked alerts with severity mappings (P0/P1) and on-call rotations updated
Security: credential rotations, KMS keys validated, and audit logging confirmed
Playbook: communication templates (customer notice, internal incident) prepared in Google Drive
Capacity: autoscaler thresholds tuned and minimum pool reserved for launch window
Fallback: lower-cost compatible model variants registered with automatic routing fallback
Billing: preflight budget cap set and billing alert configured for +10% over expected
kpi_thresholds: Latency p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 450ms (per-route SLA targets)
Quality regression: prompt-suite A mean BLEU/ROUGE delta <= -1.5 relative to baseline or human review flag
Token cost change <= +15% vs baseline during ramp; if > +15% trigger cost investigation
Adoption: successful requests per minute increase follows exponential ramp model; deviation > 20% triggers capacity review
traffic_and_capacity_probes: Preflight synthetic sweep: 100 qps for 15m across short/long prompts to exercise KV cache behavior
Canary profile: 1% of production traffic for 2 hours then 6 hours of steady-state observation
Burst test: spike to 5x normal qps for 5 minutes with circuit-breaker monitoring
Cache warmup probe: send cold prefixes to validate KV cache population time < 60s
Batching stress: 10k small requests per minute to ensure batching does not inflate latency beyond p95 target
contingency_triggers: If p99 latency > 600ms for 5 consecutive minutes -> slow-path flag and immediate shift to fallback model variant
If 5xx rate > 0.5% for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows -> pause ramp and initiate incident bridge
If quality regression threshold exceeded -> rollback to previous model version and start gated review
If token cost exceeds +25% budget cap -> throttle non-critical routes and open cost war room
Manual abort condition: >3 customer-impacting errors reported within 30m -> full rollback and postmortem schedule
rollout_phases: Phase 0 (smoke): internal test groups only, sanity checks (T-7)
Phase 1 (closed canary): 1% prod traffic, automated guards (T-6 to T-3)
Phase 2 (gradual ramp): 10% -> 30% -> 60% with 1h stabilization steps (Go window)
Phase 4 (normalize): reduce monitoring cadence to baseline and close launch room
owner_responsibilities: Product Ops (Marisol): runbook owner, final go/no-go decision maker
SRE (Ethan): capacity verification, autoscaler tuning, rollback automation
Applied ML (Priya): quality gate ownership, prompt-suite evaluation updates
Platform Eng (Liam): routing rules, canary config, network fallbacks
Customer Success (Sofia): customer comm templates, priority customer watchlist
communication_plan: Hourly status: set message template with KPIs snapshot (latency, errors, cost, quality)
Stakeholder update cadence: 3x updates in first 6 hours post-go (0h, +3h, +6h)
Customer-facing note: prepared short template and escalation contact list
automation_and_checks: Preflight CI job that runs synthetic suite and blocks go if regressions found (job: preflight/signal-sentinel)
Autoscale smoke test with canary instances spun up via infra pipeline
Automated rollback play: API call to routing layer to divert to fallback and send incident notification
Quality gating: nightly eval job that pushes deltas to alerting if model score drops beyond threshold
post_launch_actions: 7-day retrospective: capture signal misses, false positives, and refine thresholds
Update runbooks: incorporate lessons and tighten automated triggers
Customer outreach: proactive check-ins for top 10 enterprise customers
notes_to_self: Quick notes: prioritize the prompt-suite A (contains legacy edge cases). Keep the stall window short during ramp (no more than 1h at each step). Double-check that billing alerts are tested with synthetic spend. If SLOs are borderline at 30% ramp, prefer conservative rollback and do a second canary with extended observation. Leave open question: should we include an AB test for the new quantized model variant? (chat w/ Priya).
